stem: Who brought the ruins at Hampi to light in 1800 and prepared the first survey map of the site?
options: Alexander Greenlaw
Colin Mackenzie
J.F. Fleet
John Marshall
explanation: Correct option: (B). Colin Mackenzie, an engineer and antiquarian employed by the English East India Company, brought the ruins to light in 1800 and prepared the first survey map. Alexander Greenlaw took the first detailed photographs in 1856, J.F. Fleet began documenting the temple inscriptions in 1876, and conservation began under John Marshall in 1902.

stem: Which of the following best explains why Colin Mackenzie collected local histories and surveyed historic sites such as Vijayanagara?
options: To understand India's past and make governing the colony easier
To restore ruined temples so that local worship could resume
To search for treasure believed to lie under the ruined palaces
To prove that the city had been built by foreign merchants
explanation: Correct option: (A). stem: Which of the following best explains how the amara-nayaka system, an important source of the empire's military strength, also contributed to the collapse of the central imperial structure?
options: The nayakas were strictly forbidden to keep troops and so could not defend the frontiers
Nayakas who controlled revenue and armed forces could set up independent kingdoms

stem: Which of these questions about Vijayanagara can historians NOT answer merely by studying the surviving buildings?
options: How well the city was prepared to defend itself
What materials and techniques the builders used
What wages the masons and stonecutters received
How ideas spread from buildings in other regions
explanation: Correct option: (C). The chapter lists wages, the origins of the masons and the views of ordinary people among questions that buildings alone cannot answer. By contrast, fortifications reveal defence requirements, the remains show the materials and techniques used, and comparing buildings with those elsewhere reveals the spread of ideas.
